userStories.title: Add typed Collection enum + descriptor Registry (pure types, no consumers)
userStories.description: Introduce a typed registry for memory collections in `internal/storage/memoryindex/`. (a) New file `internal/storage/memoryindex/collections.go` (keep it under 200 LOC). (b) Declare `type Collection string` and 6 constants — `CollectionWiki = "wiki"`, `CollectionSource = "source"`, `CollectionArchive = "archive"`, `CollectionProposal = "proposal"`, `CollectionUserMemory = "user_memory"`, `CollectionOperational = "operational"`. Values MUST match the existing `KindSource/KindArchive/KindProposal` strings declared at `internal/storage/memoryindex/store.go:16-20` (i.e. `string(CollectionSource) == KindSource`, etc.) so back-compat lands trivially in US-L02. (c) Declare `type RetrievalMode string` with constants `RetrievalExact = "exact"`, `RetrievalFTS = "fts"`, `RetrievalVector = "vector"`, `RetrievalHybrid = "hybrid"`. (d) Declare `type CollectionDescriptor struct { Kind Collection; Label string; Description string; DefaultMode RetrievalMode; ParentCollection Collection (empty for root); StorageBackend string }` — `StorageBackend` is a stable token like `compact_memory_documents`, `wiki_documents`, `proposed_updates` so future projection-freshness work has a join key. (e) Declare `var Registry = map[Collection]CollectionDescriptor{...}` populated with all 6 entries. Use realistic descriptions cribbed from the audit doc §A.1-A.4 — Wiki/Source/Archive/Proposal are concrete today; UserMemory/Operational are scaffolded for Phase 7C/7D (note this in their Description). (f) Helper `func Lookup(k Collection) (CollectionDescriptor, bool)`. (g) NO consumer changes: do not touch store.go, rebuild.go, search.go, memory_search.go in this story. (h) Table-driven test `collections_test.go` covers: every Collection constant resolves to a Registry entry; the 3 historical Kind strings match exactly (`KindSource == string(CollectionSource)` etc. — assert via existing constants); UserMemory/Operational descriptors have empty StorageBackend OR a clearly stub token, and their Description names them as 'scaffolded — wired in Phase 7C/7D'; Lookup returns ok=false on unknown.

userStories.title: Preserve per-channel score components through RRF fusion (memoryindex + search)
userStories.description: Today retrieval emits a single fused float; the per-channel rank contributions are accumulated inside `entry.score` then DROPPED at `internal/storage/memoryindex/store.go:599` and `internal/storage/search/search.go:374` (per audit §D). Phase 7B's PRD §7 deliverable 'structured retrieval hits with score components' requires preserving the breakdown end-to-end. (a) Extend `memoryindex.Document` struct (`store.go:32-50` area) with three new float64 fields: `ScoreExact`, `ScoreFTS`, `ScoreVector`. The existing `Score float64` stays as the fused RRF score (no rename — back-compat). (b) Extend `search.Result` struct (`search.go:88-101`) with the same three fields. (c) Modify `mergeDocumentsRRF` (`store.go:577-622`): preserve per-channel RRF contributions by accumulating into the new fields on the merged Document — the loop currently overwrites `entry.score`; change it to ALSO write to `entry.scoreExact/scoreFTS/scoreVector` (or whichever channel matched), then surface those onto the returned Document. (d) Modify `mergeHybridResults` (`search.go:343-386`): twin change for the wiki side. (e) NO formatter changes — `memory_search.go formatMemoryResults` still emits the same single-score line; US-L04 will surface the components. (f) Test in `memoryindex/store_test.go` (or new `score_components_test.go`): build a 3-doc fixture where doc1 matches exact only, doc2 matches FTS only, doc3 matches vector only; after `mergeDocumentsRRF`, assert each doc has its corresponding channel score non-zero and the other two zero, AND `Score` (fused) is non-zero for all three. Similar test on the search side for `mergeHybridResults`. (g) Existing tests must stay green — adding fields is additive.

userStories.title: Surface score components + follow-up handles per hit in memory_search formatter
userStories.description: Make the LLM-visible retrieval output usable for both score-diagnostics AND chunk-to-parent navigation. (a) `internal/agent/tools/registry/memory_search.go formatMemoryResults` (`memory_search.go:384-451`): for each hit line, after the existing `score=X.XX` token, append `[exact=A.AA fts=B.BB vector=C.CC]` IF any of the three components is non-zero (skip the bracket entirely if all three are zero — keeps simple/historical-fixture output unchanged). Use 2-decimal precision. (b) Append a `follow_up=` token per hit naming the existing tool that would expand it. Mapping (use ONLY tool names that already exist in `internal/agent/tools/registry/`): source hit → `follow_up=read_source(source_id=<id>,mode=ocr)`; archive hit → if doc.Handle starts with `conversation:` then `follow_up=read_memory(handle=<handle>)` else `follow_up=search_memory(scope=archive,chat_id=<id>)`; wiki hit → `follow_up=[[<slug>]]` (the wiki-link syntax IS the expansion handle); proposal hit → `follow_up=read_memory(handle=proposal:<id>)`. If `read_memory` does not exist verbatim in the registry, use whichever tool name DOES exist (grep `internal/agent/tools/registry/*.go` for the canonical reader — likely `read_memory.go` or part of `memory_search.go`). DO NOT invent new tool names. (c) The `memoryResult` struct in memory_search.go (around line 217) needs to carry the 3 new score fields from US-L03 — extend it. (d) Test `memory_search_test.go`: fixture with 4 hits (1 source + 1 archive + 1 wiki + 1 proposal), each with at least one non-zero component score; assert formatter output contains the expected `[exact=… fts=… vector=…]` bracket AND the expected `follow_up=…` token for each kind. (e) Existing memory_search snapshot tests stay green for hits where ALL components are zero (the bracket is conditionally omitted).

userStories.title: SourceID filter + chunk-to-parent one-query expansion
userStories.description: Add the missing primitive for chunk-to-parent navigation: 'give me all chunks of source X in one query'. (a) Extend `memoryindex.Filter` struct (`internal/storage/memoryindex/store.go:52-56`) with a new field: `SourceID string` (empty = no filter — back-compat). (b) Wire into `filterWhere` (`store.go:507-527`): when `Filter.SourceID != ""`, append a `AND d.source_id = ?` predicate (use the same column already populated for source-kind docs at `rebuild.go:156`). (c) Expose via the LLM-facing tool: `internal/agent/tools/registry/memory_search.go` Parameters schema gains an optional `source_id` string field; when set, the tool forwards it into `Filter.SourceID`. Description text: 'Optional: scope results to chunks of this source (use the src_xxx ID from an earlier hit to walk the same document)'. (d) Test in `internal/storage/memoryindex/store_test.go`: fixture with 2 sources × 3 pages each = 6 source docs; query with `Filter{SourceID: src_A.ID}` returns exactly the 3 docs of source A in page order; query with empty SourceID still returns all 6. (e) Tool-level test in `memory_search_test.go`: pass `source_id` arg, verify the resulting hits all share `SourceID == passed_id`. (f) NO changes to non-source Kind behavior — SourceID filter is a NO-OP for archive/proposal docs (they don't carry a source_id), so existing archive/proposal tests stay green.
